### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **57** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `25748d7d21a3736bcd2fc4c9ab9cc3342a9550b2` — the merge of head `2d6842351043f14b71c34f30bc7e373eddef5e98` into base `ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 25748d7d21a3736bcd2fc4c9ab9cc3342a9550b2 && git checkout 25748d7d21a3736bcd2fc4c9ab9cc3342a9550b2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c 2d6842351043f14b71c34f30bc7e373eddef5e98 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c && git merge --no-ff 2d6842351043f14b71c34f30bc7e373eddef5e98

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review of #32059 (#31971 PR-2, `Fixes #31971`) at head 2d684235: PASS.** It lands once CI is green and the seat ACCEPTs. Two readings for #31698 PR-2 are recorded below.

- **Red line 1, never loosen: holds.** Every identity that was read by name now additionally requires the platform holder (`permissionSetHolderIsPlatform`).
  - A package with no `getPackage`, or a lookup that throws, answers "not the platform", which is fail-closed.
  - A registry without the package-scoped slice answers as `main` does, by name. That is not a loosening; #32076 owns failing closed there.
  - Standing is anchored only on the platform's `admin_full_access`, and another package's set of that name no longer crosses the tenant wall.
  - The tenant-admin rung reads rows in force by holder.
  - The delegated gate's allowlist resolves to addresses from the package of the scope's own set, and a grant is judged at both its column holder and its seam holder.
- **Red line 2, never guess: holds.**
  - The catalog-less `resolveByName` refuses a name with two listed holders. It grants nothing from any source (it marks the name `seen` before the bootstrap and the loader), and it logs every holder. That discharges this card's obligation path 1.
  - `platformPermissionSet` takes the one platform holder, and two platform holders give no answer.
- **Red line 3, independently releasable: holds.** CONTROL `/auth/me/permissions` is byte-identical to the step-0 baseline (`157f2261…`). One holder per name, which the install gate still keeps, answers as before. `Clause-②: no` is correct.

**Readings carried to #31698 PR-2** (the PR that lets a second holder exist). Neither blocks this PR.
1. **organization-delete is not "stricter" by name.** Its owned-rows count excludes every grant *named* `organization_admin*`, and `removeOrganizationAuthStructure` deletes them by name. Once another package can hold that name, that package's grants would be undercounted, so the delete would no longer be refused for them, and they would then be deleted. Today phase 1 refuses the second holder, so the PR is right that nothing changes. Before #31698 PR-2 narrows, both must count and delete only the platform holder's grants (the `permission_set_package` column, read as `grantNamesPlatformPermissionSet` reads it). The other name-only keeps are genuinely denials or over-listing: the agent strip, the boundary denylist, the bootstrap scan, the auto-grant lookup and the owner audit.
2. **`sys` as the platform test.** `sys` is a shareable namespace (`isShareableNamespace`). The predicate is sound only while a non-platform package in `sys` can never hold a platform set's name beside the platform. The B shape keeps base/system/sys refused ("not widened"); #31698 PR-2 must keep that, and pin it: a second `sys` package that declares `admin_full_access` is refused at install.

- **Form:** draft to `main`, `Fixes #31971`, the second half of the split in amendment 6753920432 that PR-1 (#32027) began. `Clause-②: no`, `Narrowing: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch changeset.

That covers `admin_full_access` status and cross-tenant, config and org admin, explain, approval override, last-admin-guard, default-org owner binding, role change, upgrade-report recipients, and catalog-set-in-effect.
  - **Delegated-admin gate.** It compares `(package, name)`. The allow-list resolves to addresses through the scope-carrying set's package, and grants are judged on both the column holder and the seam-stamped holder. Position and containment checks work the same way.
  - **Catalog-less arm.** `resolveByName` refuses two holders, grants nothing, and warns naming every holder. This is epic obligation path 1.
  - **Kept by name on purpose** (each refuses or over-lists, as recorded in the Acceptance notes): agent stripping, the org-boundary refusal table, the admin count on org delete (corrected by #31698 PR-2, as above), the bootstrap scan, auto-grant dedup and the owner audit warning. `verify rls.ts` is unchanged because its probe already resolves with no caller, matching the seam.
- **CONTROL:** byte-identical to the step-0 baseline (sha256 `157f2261…`).
- **Pins and ablations:** 21 new pins (plugin-security 16, plugin-auth 5) and 10 ablations, all red and then restored (`server-seat3/31971-pr2/ablations.txt`). The dogfood refusal text names the package only when the allow-list holds this set's name under another package.
- **Gates:** `check-governed-merges --branch` reports NOT governed (0 of 19 paths), +1001/−89. K = 13, and a local merge with `main` is clean. dispatch-gates 83/83 exit 0, with none unrun, and lint passes. CI on this head: 70 runs, 57 success, 13 skipped, none failed.
- **Landing:** ready, with auto-merge in this stroke. On merge: the #31971 landing record, then #31698 PR-2 is unblocked.
